title: Repurposing Regulatory Rodent Toxicology Safety Archives to Identify Candidate Hormetic Longevity Agents Highlights Emergent Mitochondrial Mechanisms.
label: approved
note: Candidate longevity compounds from toxicology archives, not diet.
abstract: Efforts to extend longevity and healthspan have benefited from the use of in vitro systems, short-lived model organisms and computational approaches, but translation to humans depends on demonstrating efficacy and safety in mammalian in vivo models. However, rigorously controlled rodent lifespan studies are slow, costly and low-throughput. Hormesis, the induction of adaptive stress response pathways by low-level toxic or metabolic challenges, provides a mechanistic means for improved resilience, but testing hormetic dose-response relationships in mammals is logistically challenging. Regulatory long-term toxicity studies, mandated for chemical authorisation, routinely generate lifespan and chronic toxicity data from large cohorts across multiple dose groups and therefore represent an underused resource for detecting unexpected survival benefits. We mined a random subset of the German Federal Institute for Risk Assessment (BfR) electronic archive for long-term rodent pesticide studies in ≥ 50 animals per dose and sex. From qualifying studies with 154 substances, we identified 27 substances (18% of entries) that significantly increased survival at study termination (≥ 10%, p < 0.05). Fifteen publicly disclosable substances were examined further; roughly half perturbed mitochondrial oxygen consumption rates in mammalian cells, and bromoxynil acted as a mitochondrial uncoupler. Back-translation to Caenorhabditis elegans showed bromoxynil improved multiple healthspan indicators without compromising organismal health. Regulatory toxicity archives can thus be repurposed to identify candidate compounds, targets and mechanisms for mammalian healthy ageing research, complement conventional screening pipelines, align with 3Rs by maximising existing data, and supply high-quality datasets for AI-driven prioritisation of interventions for rigorous preclinical follow-up.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with anemia among adolescents in Uganda: a cross-sectional analysis of a national survey.
label: approved
abstract:
Background

Previous studies have reported high rates of anemia among adolescents in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). It is unclear whether anemia rates have improved following temporal improvements in national investments by government and nutrition programs. The aim of this study was to establish the prevalence and factors associated with anemia among adolescents in a nationally representative survey.

Methods

This was a cross-sectional study to determine the prevalence and predictors of anemia in adolescents aged 10-19 years. We analyzed data from the Nutrition Module of the 2018/2019 Uganda National Panel Survey (UNPS) and included 1063 adolescents with hemoglobin measurements who participated in the 2018/2019 survey. We determined the proportion of adolescents (and 95% confidence intervals, CIs) with anemia using WHO cutoffs. We used bivariable followed by multivariable Poisson regression model with robust variance to determine associated factors. QGIS software was used for spatial analysis.

Results

Of the 119,148 participants in the 2018/2019 UNPS dataset, 24,856 were adolescents, 1063 of whom had hemoglobin measurements were included in the analysis. Overall, 172 adolescents (16.2%, CI 14%-19%) had anemia, 124(11.7%) of whom had mild anemia, 43(4.1%) had moderate anemia, and 5(0.5%) had severe anemia. The prevalence of anemia was 1.77 [aPR 1.83, CI 1.39-2.41] times high in males than in females. Adolescents aged 15-19 years were 1.99 times [aPR 1.97 CI 1.48-2.61)] more likely to be anemic than adolescents aged 10-14 years. Helicobacter pylori infection positivity increased the prevalence of anemia (aPR = 1.87, 95% CI = 1.35-2.58). There were no significant regional differences in anemia prevalence.

Conclusion

The prevalence of anemia in adolescents remains high in Uganda and is possibly associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. Anemia was paradoxically more prevalent in males than in females suggesting a recent shift in burden. Anemia and Helicobacter pylori screening and prevention should be integrated into adolescent and school health programmes in Uganda and should equally target males and females.

title: Myeloid-Derived Growth Factor Alleviates Diabetic Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease by Up-Regulating ABCA1 and ABCG1 Expression via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα Pathway.
label: approved
abstract: The regulatory role of bone marrow in systemic metabolic processes remains incompletely characterized. Myeloid-derived growth factor (MYDGF) is a myeloid cell-secreted factor with emerging metabolic functions, but its action in diabetes-associated non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (DM NAFLD) is undefined. To investigate the influence of myeloid cell-derived MYDGF on DM NAFLD, both loss- and gain-of-function approaches were applied in vivo. DM NAFLD models were established in Mydgf-knockout (KO) mice, Pparg<sup>ΔLyz2</sup> mice and Pparg<sup>ΔLyz2</sup>/KO (DKO) mice. For in vitro studies, primary Kupffer cells (KCs) were stimulated with high glucose and recombinant MYDGF (rMYDGF) and bone marrow cells (BMCs) were co-cultured with KCs via a transwell system. Protein levels related to DM NAFLD pathology and signalling pathways were quantified. In this study, we found that MYDGF was significantly downregulated in DM NAFLD mouse liver. Myeloid MYDGF deficiency exacerbated hepatic inflammation, lipogenesis, steatosis and macrophage infiltration, while reconstituting myeloid MYDGF reversed these phenotypes. rMYDGF attenuated inflammation, reduced macrophage foaming, decreased cholesterol content and increased efferocytosis. Mechanistically, MYDGF induced AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) phosphorylation, which subsequently activated the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ)/liver X receptor α (LXRα) pathway in KCs and upregulated downstream ABCA1 and ABCG1 expression. These results identify the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα-ABCA1/ABCG1 cascade as the core signalling axis mediating MYDGF's metabolic regulatory effects, which bridges the previously unrecognized functional linkage between myeloid cell function and hepatic lipid homeostasis, and explains the protective phenotype observed in MYDGF-reconstituted DM NAFLD mice. In conclusion, myeloid cell-derived MYDGF ameliorates DM NAFLD, decreases cholesterol content in macrophages and reduces lipid accumulation via the AMPK/PPARγ/LXRα pathway. MYDGF serves as a key mediator for bone marrow-liver metabolic crosstalk, indicating that the bone marrow may act as a potential endocrine target for the prevention and treatment of diabetes-related metabolic disorders.

title: Right ventricular infarction with a culprit lesion in the distal right coronary artery: incidence and clinical characteristics.
label: approved
abstract:
Objectives

Right ventricular infarction (RVI) is commonly observed in patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction and typically results from proximal right coronary artery (RCA) occlusion. However, the occurrence of RVI and its clinical characteristics in patients with distal RCA lesions are not well defined.

Methods

We retrospectively investigated 128 patients with inferior ST-elevation myocardial infarction caused by RCA occlusion who underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention at our institution between January 2020 and December 2023. RVI was diagnosed based on echocardiographic evidence and hemodynamic instability. Clinical characteristics and incidence rates were compared between patients with RVI [the RVI (+) group] and those without RVI [the RVI (-) group]. Findings on coronary angiography were assessed in detail for patients with distal RCA lesions.

Results

RVI was identified in 24/128 patients (18.8%), including 3/31 patients (9.7%) with distal RCA lesions. Right ventricular global longitudinal strain (RVGLS) was significantly lower in the RVI (+) group (-14.0% [-16.4, -11.6] vs. -16.4% [-18.7, -13.9]; p=0.004), as was right ventricular free wall strain (RVFWS) (-14.7% [-18.5, -10.6] vs. -17.7% [-20.7, -15.0]; p=0.01). RVGLS and RVFWS values were comparable in the RVI (+) group regardless of whether the RCA lesion was distal or proximal. There was no significant difference in TIMI flow before or after percutaneous coronary intervention or in the distribution of lesions.

Conclusions

RVI can be caused by distal RCA lesions, albeit less often than by proximal RCA lesions. No significant differences in RV strain parameters were observed between distal and proximal lesions.

title: Peak Cardiac Mechanical and Haemodynamic Responses During Incremental Exercise Are Temporally Associated With Ventilatory Thresholds: Novel Insight Into the Coordination of Integrative Physiological Responses to Exercise.
label: approved
note: Exercise physiology in healthy young adults; kept, low relevance, since Triage keeps papers when unsure.
abstract:
Background

Maximal aerobic capacity (VO2peak) is traditionally attributed to limitations in oxygen transport and utilization. However, it remains unclear whether peak cardiac mechanical and haemodynamic responses occur in temporal association to ventilatory thresholds during incremental exercise, and whether these relationships vary with cardiorespiratory fitness.

Methods

Eighteen healthy, recreationally active adults (26 ± 3.18 years VO2peak 41.87 ± 4.76 mL·kg·min-1) completed two incremental supine cycling tests to exhaustion, with breath-by-breath gas exchange analysis, exercise echocardiography, and continuous blood pressure monitoring. Plateau timing (PT) was defined as the relative heart rate (%HRmax) at which each cardiovascular variable reached its peak or plateau response. Associations between cardiovascular PTs, VO2peak, and the first (VT1) and second ventilatory thresholds (VT2) were examined using correlation analysis. Exploratory k-means clustering was used to descriptively visualize plateau-timing distributions.

Results

VT1 significantly correlated with PT-ejection fraction (EF) and PT-vascular conductance, whereas VT2 correlated with deformation-based parameters including PT-apical circumferential strain, PT-apical rotation, and iCarT (p < 0.05). VO2peak was positively associated with PT-twist and PT-apical rotation (p < 0.05), and negatively associated with PT-EF (p < 0.05). Exploratory clustering yielded two descriptive clusters which differed in VO2peak (p < 0.05) and were characterized by differences in volumetric and rotational plateau-timing distributions.

Conclusions

During exercise, different cardiac parameters are temporally associated with ventilatory thresholds 1 and 2. Cardiorespiratory fitness may influence interindividual differences in the temporal organization of response patterns during incremental exercise.

title: Liver Injury Due to Hormonal Contraceptives in the Modern Era.
label: approved
abstract:
Background and aims

Hormonal agents and their association with liver injury remain a concern in clinical practice. This study aimed to characterise the biochemical and clinical features of hormonal agent-associated liver injury and compare them with a control group of age- and gender-matched cases of liver injury caused by non-hormonal drugs.

Methods

Of 2123 adjudicated drug-induced liver injury cases enrolled in the Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network (2004-2024), 20 high-confidence cases (1.3%) were attributed to hormonal agents. These cases were compared with age- and sex-matched non-hormonal drug-induced liver injury (DILI) controls, and analyses assessed clinical features, biochemical patterns, outcomes, HLA alleles and candidate genetic variants associated with cholestatic liver disease.

Results

The median age of women was 22 years. Most presented within 2-12 weeks with jaundice and pruritus, predominantly with cholestatic or mixed patterns of liver enzyme elevations, but a hepatocellular pattern was not uncommon at 28%. The route of administration did not appear to influence DILI risk. Half underwent a liver biopsy, and half required hospitalization, but none died or required liver transplantation. Compared with other DILI cases, hormonal agent-associated liver injury was more often cholestatic, with jaundice and pruritus, and less frequently associated with fever or rash. No HLA association was identified, although the intronic MROH2A variant rs6722064 ranked as the top potential candidate for increased risk [OR (95% CI) = 3.58 (1.67, 7.65), p = 0.001].

Conclusions

Hormonal agent-associated liver injury presents with a distinctive mixed or cholestatic pattern and often lacks the inflammatory features seen in other DILI cases. These findings underscore the need for greater clinical awareness to improve patient outcomes.

title: Prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension in South Asians: Evidence from a national survey of Sri Lanka.
label: approved
note: Hypertension risk factors including salt intake; kept, low relevance, since Triage keeps papers when unsure.
abstract:
Background

Blood pressure(BP) control remains suboptimal worldwide. Sex-related disparities in hypertension have been reported, but data from South Asia are limited. Understanding the epidemiology and sex-related differences is essential to improve BP control.

Objectives

To assess the prevalence, associations and sex-related disparities of hypertension among Sri Lankans.

Methods

We analysed secondary data from the Sri Lanka STEPS Survey 2021, a nationally representative, community-based, cross-sectional study. Hypertension was defined as BP ≥ 140/90 mmHg or current antihypertensive use; controlled BP as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Prevalences, associations, and sex-related disparities in hypertension, undiagnosed hypertension, and BP control were assessed using logistic regression.

Results

Data from 4,634 adults(mean age 43.5(weighted CI 43.0-44.1) years; female 54.8 (53.1-56.5)%) were analysed. Overall, 37.2(35.5-38.9)% had hypertension, of whom 60.0(58.1-63.4) % were previously undiagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 73.6 (73.6, 69.6-77.2)% were on treatment, but only 38.0(33.0-44.20)% achieved BP targets. The rates of hypertension prevalence (p = 0.600), treated hypertension (p = 0.398), and controlled blood pressure (p = 0.819) in females and males did not differ significantly by sex. However, undiagnosed hypertension was significantly higher in males (69.4%, 65.3-73.1) than in females (53.6%, 50.1-57.0) (p < 0.001). Differences in the associations of hypertension by sex were noted; diabetes was associated only in females (p < 0.001), while wealth quintile (p < 0.001) and 24-hour urinary salt excretion (p = 0.011) were associated only in males. Overweight/obesity was shown to have a significant association with undiagnosed hypertension only in males (p = 0.017) in stratified analyses.

Conclusions

More than half of the hypertensives in this South Asian population were previously undiagnosed. Of hypertensives, ¾ were treated, but only 1/3 achieved treatment goals. Prevalence, treatment and control rates of hypertension were not different between females and males, but undiagnosed hypertension was more common in men. Therefore, the emphasis should be on improving the detection of hypertension, especially in men, and on treating to targets in both sexes.

title: Adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion in women with premature ovarian insufficiency receiving hormone replacement therapy: protocol for a multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial.
label: approved
abstract:
Introduction

Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) is characterized by impaired ovarian function before 40 years of age and is associated with menstrual disturbance, infertility, hypoestrogenic symptoms, psychological distress, and long-term health risks. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) is recommended for symptom control and prevention of estrogen-deficiency-related complications but does not reliably restore ovarian activity or fertility potential. Acupuncture and moxibustion are used as complementary interventions for ovarian dysfunction; however, evidence regarding their independent and combined adjunctive effects in women with POI remains limited.

Methods

This prospective, multicenter, assessor-blinded, 2 × 2 factorial randomized controlled trial will recruit 144 women with POI from three clinical centers. Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to estradiol/dydrogesterone alone, acupuncture plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone, or combined acupuncture and moxibustion plus estradiol/dydrogesterone. The intervention period will last 12 weeks. The primary outcome is the change from baseline to week 12 in antral follicle count (AFC). Secondary outcomes include serum anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH), sex hormones, ovarian hemodynamic parameters, menopausal and anxiety symptoms, Traditional Chinese Medicine syndrome scores, and menstrual status. Clinical pregnancy will be analyzed as an exploratory reproductive outcome during treatment and follow-up at weeks 24 and 48. Factorial models will estimate the main effects of acupuncture and moxibustion, whereas the acupuncture × moxibustion interaction will be considered exploratory.

Conclusion

This trial will evaluate the adjunctive effects of acupuncture and moxibustion on AFC and related secondary clinical outcomes in a selected subgroup of women with POI receiving standard HRT. The factorial design will permit estimation of the independent effects of both interventions and exploratory assessment of their potential interaction.

Clinical trial number

https://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier ITMCTR2025002408.

title: Prognostic value of the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte index for predicting one-year mortality in acute pulmonary embolism.
label: approved
abstract:
Background and objectives

Acute pulmonary embolism (APE) is associated with substantial mortality despite advances in diagnosis and treatment. Biomarkers reflecting inflammation, immune status, and nutritional reserve may improve risk stratification. This study aimed to evaluate the prognostic significance of the C-reactive protein-albumin-lymphocyte (CALLY) index for predicting one-year mortality in patients with APE and to compare its performance with the Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) and Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII).

Methods

This retrospective single-center study included 471 consecutive patients diagnosed with APE between July 2021 and December 2024. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. CALLY, PNI, and SII were calculated using admission laboratory parameters. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis and Cox regression models were performed to evaluate the prognostic performance of these indices.

Results

During one-year follow-up, 102 patients (21.7%) died. CALLY values were significantly lower in non-survivors than in survivors (p < 0.001). CALLY demonstrated the highest discriminatory performance for one-year mortality (AUC 0.787, 95% CI 0.732-0.842), compared with PNI (AUC 0.728) and SII (AUC 0.643). CALLY remained independently associated with one-year mortality after multivariable adjustment (HR 0.904, 95% CI 0.856-0.955; p < 0.001). Furthermore, adding CALLY to a baseline model including age, sPESI ≥1, elevated cardiac troponin, and sPAP increased the C-statistic from 0.700 to 0.739 and significantly improved model fit (likelihood-ratio p < 0.001).

Conclusions

The CALLY index was independently associated with one-year all-cause mortality in patients with APE and demonstrated higher discriminatory performance than PNI and SII. As a simple index derived from routinely available laboratory parameters, CALLY may provide additional prognostic information for long-term risk assessment in APE.

title: Dating the Colonisation and Source of Adaptive Genetic Variation in the Iago Sparrow (Passer iagoensis).
label: approved
abstract: Ancestral adaptive variation is thought to play an important role in facilitating adaptation to insular environments. However, to properly evaluate its role, we need to determine the age of genetic variation. In this study, we investigate the Iago sparrow (Passer iagoensis), a generalist endemic to the Cabo Verde archipelago, to understand how genetic diversity is maintained in an island lineage where populations are likely ephemeral and adaptation to environmental extremes is ongoing. Using whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic data, we inferred the species' evolutionary history, population structure, and signatures of selection. Our results show that the Iago sparrow diverged from its closest mainland relative approximately 4.26 million years ago, although the colonisation likely occurred only around 2 million years ago. Population structure analyses reveal three distinct lineages, corresponding to geographic divisions within the archipelago, with the Rombos islets population exhibiting significant phenotypic divergence, particularly in bill morphology. Genome scans and phenotypic measurements identified signatures of divergent selection in genes associated with bill size (HMG20B) and bill shape (ALX1), suggesting adaptive evolution in response to local environmental conditions. Our ancestral recombination graph analysis provided temporal estimates for adaptive variation associated with these genes, suggesting that adaptive haplotypes observed in the Rombos population arose after colonisation of the archipelago. This contrasts with patterns described in Darwin's finches, where ancestral variation likely originated prior to colonisation. Our findings highlight the interplay of genetic drift, gene flow, and selection in shaping island species' genetic diversity. The Iago sparrow, a generalist thriving across diverse habitats, provides insights into the mechanisms that maintain genetic diversity in island lineages despite small population sizes and pronounced environmental heterogeneity.

title: Chemodectoma Arising From the Abdominal Aorta in a 9-Year-Old Female Dog: Clinical, Histopathological and Immunohistochemstric Study.
label: approved
abstract:
Background

Chemodectomas are uncommon, typically benign neoplasms derived from paraganglionic chemoreceptor tissues, most frequently arising in the heart base or carotid bodies of brachycephalic dogs. This report documents a detailed pathological description of a chemodectoma originating from the abdominal aorta in a non-human species, representing, to our knowledge, the first case specifically characterized by its origin at the aortic trifurcation, thereby expanding the recognized anatomical spectrum of this tumour entity.

Case presentation

A 9-year-old spayed female terrier was presented with persistent panting, recent-onset obesity following previous cachexia, and a complex clinical history including polyuria/polydipsia and pyoderma. Haematological and biochemical analyses revealed a regenerative anaemia, leucocytosis, and biochemical indicators suggestive of cholestasis and potential endocrinopathy. Advanced imaging identified a solitary, well-demarcated, highly vascular abdominal mass closely associated with the aortic trifurcation. Given the tumour's inaccessibility and pronounced vascularity, cytological confirmation via fine needle aspiration was precluded due to haemorrhagic risk, necessitating exploratory laparotomy.

Management and outcome

Intraoperatively, the mass was unresectable because of its anatomical relationships and the prohibitive risk of catastrophic haemorrhage. Humane euthanasia was subsequently elected. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated a lobulated neoplasm composed of pleomorphic neuroendocrine cells, with low mitotic activity and an absence of necrosis or haemorrhage. Immunohistochemistry confirmed strong, diffuse synaptophysin reactivity and focal neuron-specific enolase positivity, while chromogranin A and S100 protein were negative, underscoring immunophenotypic variability.

Conclusion

This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity and therapeutic limitations posed by extra-cardiac chemodectomas in veterinary species, especially when located in unconventional anatomical sites. Limitations included the unavailability of computed tomography and lack of postoperative follow-up. This report expands the recognized clinico-pathological spectrum of chemodectomas and highlights the necessity for multidisciplinary diagnostic strategies and further research aimed at defining optimal management protocols for such rare and challenging presentations.

title: Emotion Regulation Difficulties Account for the Associations Between Childhood Maltreatment and Perceived Stress in Young Adulthood.
label: approved
abstract:
Childhood exposure to traumatic events can have enduring negative effects, particularly on stress perception and overall well-being. Emotion dysregulation, which refers to difficulties in managing emotional responses, is frequently observed among individuals with a history of interpersonal trauma and has been proposed as a construct linking childhood maltreatment to heightened stress in adulthood. Using an Associational Variable Analysis (AVA), this study examined whether emotion regulation difficulties accounted for shared variance between childhood maltreatment and perceived stress in adulthood. A sample of 351 university students completed self-report assessments of childhood maltreatment (CTQ), emotion regulation difficulties (DERS), and perceived stress (PSS-10). At the total-score level, emotion regulation difficulties significantly accounted for the association between emotional neglect and perceived stress, whereas emotional abuse and sexual abuse maintained direct associations with stress. At the subscale level, specific emotion regulation difficulties accounted for the associations of emotional abuse and emotional neglect with both perceived helplessness and perceived self-efficacy, with limited access to emotion regulation strategies and difficulties engaging in goal-directed behavior emerging as the most relevant regulatory dimensions. These findings highlight emotion regulation difficulties as an important construct linking childhood emotional maltreatment with perceived stress in adulthood, while emphasizing the need for longitudinal designs before causal conclusions can be drawn.

Supplementary information

The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40653-026-00946-8.

title: Multi-segment intussusception in infant with suspected celiac crisis: A case report.
label: approved
abstract: Celiac crisis (CC) is a rare, life-threatening manifestation of often undiagnosed or inadequately treated celiac disease (CeD). In infants with nonclassical presentations of CeD, timely diagnosis can be challenging but critical to reducing end-organ damage and serious complications, such as CC. We report a case of a 14-month-old infant presenting with 1 month of inappetence, malnutrition, and abdominal pain in the absence of diarrhea. The infant was found to have extraintestinal manifestations suggestive of CC, such as electrolyte derangement, hypoalbuminemia, and neurologic dysfunction. However, the infant also presented with unusual multi-segment small bowel-small bowel intussusception prior to the diagnosis of CeD. Intussusception may reflect severe small bowel enteropathy in CeD. Hypoalbuminemia and intestinal edema seen in CC may further precipitate small bowel-small bowel intussusception. Future studies should clarify distinct phenotypes of infantile-onset CeD associated with more severe CC.

title: Mapping five decades of high-intensity interval training research (1977-2026): database sensitivity, intellectual structure, and thematic development.
label: approved
note: Bibliometric map of HIIT research; kept, low relevance, since Triage keeps papers when unsure.
abstract:
Objective

To characterize HIIT research while testing how database membership, document eligibility, and keyword metadata affect bibliometric representations of the field.

Methods

Archived Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and PubMed exports were reconstructed through documented deduplication and retrospective computational metadata screening. The primary corpus comprised 7,141 research articles published from 1977 to the March 2026 snapshot. Analyses included database sensitivity, Bradford zones and cumulative-model fit, identifier-based Lotka estimation, source-specific citations, WoS reference co-citation, author-keyword mapping, volume-balanced thematic periods, and Scopus affiliation-country collaboration.

Results

Of 18,578 record instances, 8,365 unique records remained after deduplication; 1,224 were excluded under the documented rules. Annual output increased from 80 articles in 2013 to 898 in 2025. Scopus membership covered 94.17% of the primary union, compared with 71.63% for WoS and 71.92% for PubMed. Top-20 keyword sets were similar across single-source subsets (Jaccard = 0.905-1.000), whereas keyword-field and network-size choices produced 3-8 themes. The 19 core journal identities contributed 33.61% of articles. Among 24,074 Scopus author identifiers, the estimated Lotka exponent was β = 2.447; both the fitted and classical full-range models failed bootstrap goodness-of-fit tests (p = 0.001). WoS co-citation identified four strongly interconnected reference communities, and the primary author-keyword map contained seven themes. Including reviews increased the corpus to 8,074 and the PubMed-only contribution from 166 to 876 records.

Conclusion

Broad topic visibility was comparatively stable, but database-specific contributions and thematic granularity depended on eligibility and metadata decisions. Source-resolved indicators and explicit sensitivity analyses provide a more defensible representation than an unqualified merged-data map. Findings describe bibliographic structure, not intervention effectiveness; historical search-date precision and independent screening agreement remain limitations.

title: Mineral-Enriched Biochars from Co-Pyrolysis of Sewage Sludge, Sawdust, and Basaltic Rocks: Soil Amendment Potential and Carbon Stability.
label: approved
abstract: Co-pyrolysis of sewage sludge (SS) and sawdust (SD) with basaltic minerals may produce nutrient-enriched biochars for soil amendment and long-term carbon (C) persistence. However, the effects of mineral incorporation on C transformations and the interpretation of conventional stability indices remain poorly understood. To address this gap, we compared SS and SD copyrolyzed with zeolitic basalt (ZB) and metabasalt (MB). The resulting materials, produced at 500 °C, were characterized by proximate and elemental analyses, X-ray diffraction, energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and nutrient and carbon-stability assessments. Mineral addition increased biochar yields to 70-73%, whereas SD-derived biochar exhibited the highest fixed C and thermostable fractions. Materials obtained by co-pyrolyzing SD with ZB or MB, and SS with ZB, showed high thermal resistance. Mineral-enriched biochars had higher ash contents and contained silicate-rich phases, modifying their mineralogical composition and nutrient profiles. Co-pyrolysis of SS with basaltic materials increased Ca, Mg, P, and micronutrient contents. Contrasting responses among elemental, thermochemical, and persistence-based indices showed that no single approach adequately evaluates C stability in mineral-enriched biochars. These findings support the potential use of mineral-enriched biochars as soil amendments and show that C stability requires integrated evaluation.

title: Stroke disability burden and rehabilitation service-capacity proxies in China, 1990-2023: A population-based analysis using GBD 2023 and national service statistics.
label: approved
abstract: China's stroke burden is increasingly shaped by survival with disability, population ageing, and demand for rehabilitation and long-term support. Yet the extent to which stroke disability burden has shifted towards older-old and oldest-old adults, and how this burden relates to community and elder-care service capacity, remains insufficiently quantified. We conducted a population-based secondary analysis of Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 estimates for China from 1990 to 2023, focusing on ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage. We examined disability-adjusted life years (DALYs), years lived with disability (YLDs), YLD share of DALYs, age-specific patterns among adults aged 50 years or older, estimated annual percentage changes (EAPCs), and three-factor decomposition of absolute DALY changes. We also linked 2023 stroke YLDs with national community health and elder-care service indicators as descriptive capacity proxies. From 1990 to 2023, the YLD share of DALYs increased from 10.5% to 22.3% for ischaemic stroke and from 1.8% to 3.3% for intracerebral haemorrhage. The crude all-age ischaemic stroke YLD rate increased by 2.75% per year (95% CI 2.68 to 2.82), while the crude all-age intracerebral haemorrhage DALY rate declined but its YLD rate and YLD share increased. Crude all-age rates were interpreted as population-level burden indicators influenced by population age structure, alongside age-stratified and decomposition analyses. Among adults aged 50 years or older, disability burden shifted towards older-old and oldest-old groups, particularly for ischaemic stroke. In 2023, combined all-age YLDs from ischaemic stroke and intracerebral haemorrhage were approximately 4.77 million, corresponding descriptively to 128.2 YLDs per community health service centre/station and 16.7 YLDs per community health bed. Stroke in China is increasingly a survivorship and disability challenge. The burden-to-capacity proxy indicators provide planning context but do not directly measure rehabilitation access, adequacy, quality, or unmet need.

title: Outcomes of sequential microvascular tissue transfer for radiation induced sequelae post mandibular reconstruction.
label: approved
abstract:
Background

Radiotherapy-related complications following mandibular reconstruction remain a major challenge in head and neck oncologic reconstruction. Although free fibula flap reconstruction has become the gold standard for segmental mandibular defects, delayed radiation-induced sequelae such as hardware exposure, contour deformity, soft tissue atrophy, fistula formation continue to affect long-term outcomes. Literature regarding the role of sequential microvascular tissue transfer in managing these complications remains limited.

Objectives

This study aims to evaluate the indications, surgical planning, recipient vessel selection, and outcomes of sequential microvascular free tissue transfer performed for radiation-induced sequelae after mandibular reconstruction.

Materials and methods

A retrospective observational study was conducted between June 2024 and December 2025 at a tertiary referral center. Patients who had previously undergone primary mandibular reconstruction using a fibula free flap followed by adjuvant radiotherapy and later developed radiation-related complications requiring secondary microvascular reconstruction were included. Demographic data, primary reconstructive details, radiation parameters, duration between radiation and complication, indications for sequential reconstruction, flap characteristics, recipient vessel selection, postoperative complications, and healing outcomes were analyzed.

Results

Ten patients were included in the study. All patients had undergone primary fibula free flap reconstruction following segmental mandibulectomy followed by sequential microvascular soft tissue reconstruction for radiation induced complications. Ipsilateral superficial temporal vessels were used as recipient vessels in all cases without using vein grafts. All flaps survived completely. Satisfactory wound healing and contour restoration were achieved in all patients.

Conclusion

Sequential microvascular reconstruction represents a reliable and effective strategy for managing radiation-induced complications following mandibular reconstruction. Volume loss can be addressed during plate removal surgery which not only achieves a stable soft tissue cover but also prevents further progression to osteoradionecrosis.

title: Neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio and short-term mortality in heart failure: an exploratory association without demonstrated superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII.
label: approved
note: Prognostic nutritional index and mortality in heart failure; nutritional status scores count as nutrition.
abstract:
Background

Systemic inflammation and greater illness severity are associated with adverse short-term outcomes in heart failure (HF). The neutrophil-to-prognostic nutritional index ratio (NPNR) combines neutrophil count with the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), a composite derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count that is influenced by inflammation and acute illness. This study examined the association of NPNR with 28-day and 90-day all-cause mortality in hospitalized patients with HF and assessed its replication in MIMIC-IV.

Methods

The analysis included 1,885 patients with calculable NPNR from the Zigong Heart Failure Database and 1,150 adult ICU patients with HF from MIMIC-IV. Log2-transformed NPNR was examined using Cox regression, Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and sensitivity analyses, including parsimonious and Firth-penalized Cox models. MIMIC-IV provided an independent clinical setting for assessing the direction of the association.

Results

In Zigong, each doubling of NPNR was associated with higher 28-day mortality (HR 1.728, 95% CI 1.130-2.642, p = 0.012) and 90-day mortality (HR 1.684, 95% CI 1.124-2.524, p = 0.012). However, the expanded models included only 32 and 36 deaths, respectively, and the tertile-based estimates had wide confidence intervals. RCS analyses suggested nonlinearity at both time horizons. NPNR AUCs were 0.727 and 0.717, with no significant superiority over PNI, NLR, or SII in DeLong comparisons. In MIMIC-IV, the continuous association was borderline significant at 28 days (HR 1.112, p = 0.049) and not statistically significant at 90 days (HR 1.081, p = 0.096). Higher NPNR tertiles were associated with greater mortality, while RCS analyses showed no clear nonlinearity.

Conclusion

Higher NPNR was associated with short-term all-cause mortality in the Zigong HF cohort, with weaker evidence in the MIMIC-IV ICU cohort. NPNR may be considered an exploratory laboratory-derived marker associated with systemic inflammation and illness severity. It did not demonstrate superior discrimination over PNI, NLR, or SII, and its incremental prognostic value remains uncertain. These findings do not support its routine use as a clinical decision tool.

title: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles for intestinal mucosal repair: mechanisms, microbiota-host interactions, and bioengineered delivery.
label: approved
abstract: Plant-derived extracellular vesicles (PDEVs) and related nanoparticle preparations are being investigated for intestinal mucosal repair. Much of the therapeutic evidence concerns heterogeneous plant-derived exosome-like nanoparticles (ELNs) isolated following plant tissue disruption; this review therefore distinguishes extracellularly released vesicles, tissue-derived nanoparticle preparations with unresolved origins, and reconstructed carriers. Building on foundational edible plant nanovesicle studies, we synthesize preclinical evidence across inflammatory control, structural repair, regenerative activity, and functional barrier recovery. Reported effects include modulation of macrophage activity, inflammasome signaling, and mucosal immune responses, reduced neutrophil-associated injury, epithelial protection, and improvements in junctional and mucus-associated barrier features. Intestinal stem cell responses and organoid formation support regenerative activity in selected studies, although durable regeneration remains insufficiently established. Uptake of plant-derived RNAs by gut microorganisms and metabolic relays involving tryptophan derivatives and short-chain fatty acids connect selected preparations to microbiota-host communication. Engineering strategies support drug and nucleic acid delivery, gastrointestinal protection, local colonic exposure, and cellular uptake. Evidence remains predominantly preclinical, with gaps in preparation identity, batch consistency, causal validation of active cargo, dose-exposure-response relationships, safety, and scalable manufacturing. Translation requires preparation-specific characterization and reproducible potency assays, together with integrated assessment of mucosal structure, regeneration, barrier function, and durability.

title: Beyond basic taste: mechanisms, measurement, and food-matrix translation of non-basic oral sensations.
label: approved
abstract: The five basic tastes-sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami-account for only part of food acceptance and quality. Non-basic oral sensations, including astringency, pungency, cooling, metallic sensation, fatty mouthfeel, oleogustus, tingling, numbing and kokumi, contribute substantially to hedonic and textural perception and are commercially important, yet remain less well characterized. This integrative critical review synthesizes mechanistic, neurophysiological, analytical and applied evidence for these nine sensations, treating pungency as two mechanistically distinct pathways, TRPV1- and TRPA1-mediated, to give ten mechanistic entries. Each entry is assessed on two distinct axes: mechanistic confidence, how strongly the principal proximal mechanism is supported by available evidence, and food-matrix translation confidence, how reliably that mechanism predicts perception in real foods. The two axes are related but not equivalent: higher confidence in the principal proximal mechanism does not by itself ensure high confidence in food-matrix translation. TRPV1-mediated pungency, TRPM8-mediated cooling, astringency and fatty mouthfeel rest on well-supported principal or proximal mechanisms, yet none of the ten entries reaches high translation confidence, while TRPA1-mediated pungency, tingling, numbing, oleogustus and kokumi are weaker on both axes. Three distinctions are emphasized: pungency is not a single mechanism; fatty mouthfeel is lubrication-based and mechanoreceptor-mediated, whereas oleogustus is a proposed fatty-acid-receptor perception that remains debated; and iron-related metallic sensation arises largely from retronasal perception of lipid-oxidation volatiles, with no specific human metallic receptor identified. The principal conclusion is that a well-supported mechanism does not by itself confer predictive power in food: matrix composition, salivary dilution and oral processing reshape perception, so dynamic and tribological methods are more ecologically valid than static intensity ratings, and these sensations warrant greater consideration in product formulation and sensory evaluation.

title: Burden, spectrum and associated factors of ocular disease among incarcerated populations in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
label: approved
abstract:
Background

Ocular morbidity remains poorly characterized among prisoners; this systematic review and meta-analysis quantified its prevalence, spectrum and associated factors across sub-Saharan Africa (SSA).

Methods

This review followed a published Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) Protocols (PRISMA-P) and searched eight databases using prespecified terms, with study selection guided by PRISMA. Data were standardized and synthesized using random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), with heterogeneity assessed using I 2 and sensitivity and condition-specific analyses used to assess variation.

Results

Six studies comprising 3,361 participants from four SSA countries, Nigeria, Uganda, Tanzania and Kenya, met the inclusion criteria. The pooled prevalence of ocular morbidity was 43.1% (95% CI: 12.4-77.1%; I 2 = 99.2%). Conjunctivitis was the most prevalent condition (23.9%; 95% CI, 10.7-40.1%), followed by refractive error (19.5%; 95% CI, 12.5-27.5%) and presbyopia (18.6%; 95% CI, 5.2-37.7%). Cataract (7.4%), glaucoma (5.6%) and corneal scar or opacity (3.0%) were less prevalent. Age >50 years (OR = 11.96; 95% CI, 5.31-26.94) and a history of ocular trauma (OR = 5.21; 95% CI, 1.52-17.87) were associated with higher odds of ocular morbidity. Longer imprisonment was associated with xerophthalmia (OR = 20.1; 95% CI, 8.3-48.8%), whereas access to food from outside prison was associated with lower odds of ocular morbidity (OR = 0.45; 95% CI, 0.26-0.79).

Conclusion

Ocular morbidity affects approximately four in ten prison inmates in SSA, with much of this burden preventable or treatable, despite considerable between-study heterogeneity and limited geographical evidence. Collectively, these findings support integrated prison eye care and standardized research to advance equitable interventions across SSA.

title: Panniculectomy With Umbilical Transposition in the Era of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: The Impact of Weight Loss Modality on Postoperative Outcomes.
label: approved
abstract:
Background

Panniculectomy is performed to address excess infraumbilical skin and soft tissue following weight loss. Weight loss can be achieved through lifestyle modifications, bariatric surgery, and pharmacologic therapies, such as glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) agonists. The impact of weight loss modality on postoperative outcomes remains unclear.

Objectives

The aim of this study was to evaluate whether the method of weight loss influences postoperative outcomes following panniculectomy.

Methods

A single-center retrospective review was conducted of patients who underwent panniculectomy between 2021 and 2025. Patients were grouped into 4 cohorts: lifestyle modifications alone, bariatric surgery, GLP-1 agonist therapy, or combined bariatric surgery and GLP-1 agonist therapy. Patients receiving abdominoplasty with extensive undermining and rectus plication were excluded. Variables of interest included patient demographics, weight loss history, comorbidities, wound-healing complications, surgical-site infection, hematoma/seroma, and hospital utilization. Multivariate logistic regression was performed to analyze postoperative complications and healthcare utilization, with statistical significance set at P < .05.

Results

A total of 281 patients met inclusion criteria (lifestyle modifications: n = 53 [18.9%]; bariatric surgery: n = 184 [65.5%]; GLP-1 agonist therapy: n = 20 (7.1%); and combined bariatric surgery and GLP-1 agonist therapy: n = 24 [8.5%]). Multivariate analysis showed no statistically significant differences in postoperative outcomes, including wound complications, surgical-site infections, seroma/hematoma, or hospital utilization.

Conclusions

Postoperative outcomes following panniculectomy may be similar regardless of weight loss method. Preoperative GLP-1 agonist therapy, alone or combined with bariatric surgery, was not associated with increased postoperative complications or healthcare utilization. Our results can help guide risk stratification and decision making for individuals pursuing panniculectomy after weight loss.

Level of evidence 3 risk

title: Boron nutrition in horticultural crops for enhancing yield and fruit quality.
label: approved
abstract: Boron (B) is an essential micronutrient involved in reproductive development, fruit growth, yield formation, and quality of horticultural crops. It contributes to cell wall integrity, membrane function, carbohydrate transport, pollen germination and pollen tube growth, fruit set, and nutrient translocation. B availability influences reproductive development, yield, and fruit quality, with both deficiency and excess adversely affecting crop performance, while optimal B nutrition can promote fruit development and quality. However, B responses vary considerably with crop species and cultivar, initial B status, application rate and source, and environmental conditions. This review critically examines the physiological and biochemical roles of B and the proposed mechanisms underlying its effects in horticultural crops, with emphasis on reproductive development, yield, fruit quality, and postharvest performance. It evaluates variability and limitations in the available evidence, particularly dose- and crop-dependent responses, and critically assesses the emerging use of nano-boron, including concerns related to phytotoxicity, environmental safety, nanoparticle stability, economic feasibility, and limited field validation. Although nano-boron has shown promising potential, current evidence remains insufficient to establish its consistent superiority over conventional B sources across horticultural crops. Key research gaps and priorities for developing safe, effective, and field-applicable B management strategies are also identified.

title: <i>Bacteroides uniformis</i>-generated ornithine alleviates alcohol-associated liver disease via Sirt4-mediated mitochondrial regulation.
label: approved
note: Probiotic bacterium for alcohol-related liver disease; fits no topic.
abstract: Gut microbiota plays a pivotal role in alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD), yet the contributions of individual bacterial strains and their metabolites remain poorly defined. Here, we analyzed 16S rDNA sequencing data from an ALD patient cohort and validated the findings using the NIAAA mouse model combined with multi-omics approaches. Bacteroides uniformis was significantly depleted in ALD patients, and supplementation with live B. uniformis alleviated ALD in mice by reducing hepatic steatosis, inflammation, and oxidative stress. Metabolomic analysis identified ornithine as a key metabolite produced by B. uniformis, and direct ornithine administration largely recapitulated the protective effects. Mechanistically, ornithine upregulated hepatic Sirt4, thereby restoring mitochondrial homeostasis, whereas pharmacological inhibition of Sirt4 abolished these effects. Dietary flaxseed oil increased intestinal B. uniformis abundance and hepatic Sirt4 expression, ameliorating ALD outcomes. These findings reveal a B. uniformis-ornithine-Sirt4 axis that modulates ALD via mitochondrial regulation and highlight potential microbial and metabolic therapeutic targets.

title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Fitness Methods on Depressive Symptoms and Glycaemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Comorbid Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Taijiquan and Baduanjin.
label: approved
note: Tai chi and Baduanjin for blood sugar and depression in type 2 diabetes.
abstract:
Aims

To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.

Methods

RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.

Results

Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.

Conclusions

This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.

Trial registration

The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

title: A low-calorie balanced diet improves hepatic steatosis and preserves skeletal muscle in obesity: evidence from clinical and experimental studies.
label: approved
note: Low-calorie diet, fatty liver and muscle in obesity.
abstract:
Background

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is closely linked to obesity, insulin resistance, and endocrine dysregulation. Although calorie restriction is widely used for metabolic control, it is often accompanied by unintended skeletal muscle loss, which may negatively affect long-term metabolic outcomes. Therefore, identifying a dietary strategy that improves metabolic health while preserving muscle mass is of clinical importance.

Methods

This study combined retrospective clinical observations with an in vivo high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mouse model to evaluate the effects of low-calorie balanced diet (LCD). Clinical data were used to assess changes in metabolic parameters and body composition. In parallel, obese mice subjected to LCD intervention were evaluated for body weight, glucose metabolism, hepatic steatosis, and skeletal muscle morphology. Gene expression related to hepatic lipid metabolism and muscle atrophy was analyzed.

Results

LCD intervention improved metabolic parameters, reduced body weight gain, and alleviated hepatic lipid accumulation in both clinical observations and the animal model. In HFD-fed mice, LCD improved glucose homeostasis and partially reversed hepatic steatosis. Importantly, skeletal muscle structure was preserved, and the expression of muscle atrophy-related genes, including MSTN, FOXO3a, and MuRF1, was reduced. In the liver, LCD decreased the expression of lipogenic genes such as SREBP-1c, FASN, and ACC, while partially restoring fatty acid oxidation-related genes including PPARα and CPT1α.

Conclusion

LCD improves metabolic dysfunction and hepatic steatosis while preserving skeletal muscle integrity in obesity. These findings provide translational evidence supporting LCD as a practical dietary strategy for MASLD management and highlight the importance of coordinated metabolic regulation between liver and skeletal muscle.

title: Association of Vitamin D Deficiency and Poor Glycemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
label: approved
note: Vitamin D status and blood sugar control.
abstract:
Background

Vitamin D deficiency is common among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and may be associated with inadequate glycemic control.

Objective

To determine the association between vitamin D deficiency and poor glycemic control among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Materials and methods

This cross-sectional study was conducted at Lady Reading Hospital (LRH), Peshawar, Pakistan, from March 2024 to February 2025 among 350 adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D (25(OH)D) and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) measurements were obtained from hospital laboratory records. Serum 25(OH)D was measured using an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), according to the laboratory standard operating procedure. Vitamin D deficiency was defined as a serum 25(OH)D level <20 ng/mL and poor glycemic control was defined as HbA1c ≥7.0%. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, the chi-square test, independent-samples t-test, and binary logistic regression. Multivariable binary logistic regression was performed to assess the independent association between vitamin D deficiency and poor glycemic control after adjustment for age, BMI, diabetes duration, hypertension, dyslipidemia, physical inactivity, dietary adherence, medication adherence, previous diabetes education, and smoking. Adjusted odds ratios (AORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported.

Results

Among 350 participants, 218 (62.29%) were vitamin D deficient and 132 (37.71%) were non-deficient. Poor glycemic control was present in 226 (64.57%) participants, while 124 (35.43%) had adequate control. Vitamin D deficiency was observed in 164 (72.57%) participants with poor glycemic control compared with 54 (43.55%) with adequate control (p <0.001). Participants with poor glycemic control had lower mean serum 25(OH)D levels than those with adequate control (16.72 ± 6.43 vs. 23.84 ± 7.16 ng/mL; p <0.001). After adjustment for the prespecified covariates listed above, vitamin D deficiency was associated with higher odds of poor glycemic control (AOR = 2.87, 95% CI: 1.76-4.68; p <0.001).

Conclusion

Vitamin D deficiency was common and was independently associated with higher odds of poor glycemic control among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. Given the cross-sectional design, this association should not be interpreted as causal, and prospective studies are needed to clarify the relationship.

title: Optimal Exercise Dose for Improving Multidimensional Health Outcomes in Colorectal Cancer Patients: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression.
label: approved
note: Exercise dose in colorectal cancer; cancer fits no topic.
abstract: This study aimed to investigate the dose-response relationships between exercise prescription parameters and a range of health outcomes in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). The following PRISMA guidelines, a systematic search of five databases was conducted. The inclusion criteria were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) of exercise interventions lasting ≥ 4 weeks in patients with CRC. Robust Variance Estimation (RVE) was used to synthesize the overall effects of exercise interventions across six outcome domains, including cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) and muscular fitness (MF). Univariable RVE regression models and MetaForest analyses were employed to examine the moderating effects of two groups of variables: exercise prescription moderators and patient background characteristics. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane tool, and the quality of evidence was evaluated using the GRADE approach. A total of 26 RCTs, involving 1731 CRC patients and 266 effect sizes, were included. CRF (ES = 0.35, p < 0.01) and MF (ES = 0.45, p < 0.01) showed statistically significant improvements. Regression analyses revealed threshold effects for both CRF and MF, with maximal improvements requiring sustained engagement in moderate-to-high intensity exercise. Subgroup analyses indicated that prehabilitation interventions were the most effective, while interventions during active treatment exhibited a decline-rebound trend over time. Based on these findings, high-frequency and moderate-to-high volume interventions with individualized load regulation are recommended during the pre-treatment phase. During active treatment, a more cautious approach is advised, involving reduced exercise volume during peak symptom periods and gradual progression during recovery.

title: Delivering balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplements to pregnant and breastfeeding women in low- and middle-income countries: A scoping review.
label: approved
abstract: In settings where more than 20% of women of reproductive age are classified as underweight, the World Health Organization recommends balanced energy and protein (BEP) supplementation during pregnancy to reduce adverse birth outcomes. However, guidance on contextually acceptable and feasible supplement delivery platforms remains limited, posing critical challenges for implementation. We synthesized literature on acceptable and feasible delivery platforms for BEP supplementation (direct evidence), as well as iron and folic acid (IFA) or multiple micronutrient supplements (MMS; indirect evidence) to pregnant and breastfeeding women (PBW) to broaden the search scope. A systematic search was conducted across five databases and grey literature to identify studies that addressed the acceptability and feasibility of BEP supplement delivery platforms in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), at facility and community levels. We identified 48 studies conducted in LMICs: 22 specifically evaluated BEP supplement delivery, while 26 evaluated IFA or MMS. In the direct evidence, home delivery (11/22) was the most frequently mentioned delivery platforms of BEP supplements followed by community-level feeding centers (provided cooked meals or take-home rations) anchored by frontline community health workers (8/22 studies) and antenatal care (ANC) at health facilities (6/22; some studies assessed multiple delivery platforms). Only four studies assessed preferred BEP delivery platforms, and PBW favored home over facility-based delivery. Authors attributed this preference to the comprehensive nutrition education and behavior change communication (BCC) provided during home delivery. Indirect evidence showed that enhancing delivery of IFA or MMS at health facilities (not specific) through strategies such as BCC and home visits may improve supplement compliance. Overall, limited evidence exists regarding market-based approaches for delivering any of these interventions. Based on existing evidence, scale-up delivery of BEP supplementation through ANC at health centers, enhanced by community health workers may be feasible in reaching PBW, especially when combined with BCC.

title: Vitamins E and C supplementation reduces hepatic lipid peroxidation and steatosis in neonatal Yucatan piglets receiving prolonged parenteral nutrition.
label: approved
note: Vitamins in newborn piglets fed intravenously; liver outcome fits no topic.
abstract: Parenteral nutrition (PN) is essential in neonatal care for many infants born prematurely or with impaired gastrointestinal function. However, prolonged PN use is associated with complications such as PN-associated liver disease and intestinal atrophy, potentially related to oxidative stress. Commercial PN lipid emulsions with fish oil are used to counteract PN-associated liver damage but may also contribute to oxidative stress due to their high content of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids. Using neonatal Yucatan miniature piglets as an established animal model for investigating PN-associated complications in neonates, this study investigated whether co-supplementation of vitamins E and C could reduce oxidative stress-related injury in the liver and small intestine during PN. The objective of this study was to determine whether supplementing a mixed-lipid emulsion (SMOFlipid®) with vitamins E and C would attenuate hepatic oxidative damage and enhance intestinal perfusion and morphology in neonatal piglets. Neonatal Yucatan piglets were surgically fitted with intravenous catheters and an indwelling blood flow probe around the superior mesenteric artery (SMA). Piglets received either standard PN (Control; n = 10) or PN supplemented with vitamins E (10 mg/kg/d) and C (100 mg/kg/d) (Vit E&C, n = 10) for ten days. Vitamin supplementation was associated with lower hepatic lipid accumulation and lipid peroxidation (P < 0.05 for both), compared with the control group. Plasma and liver vitamin E concentrations were markedly higher in the Vit E&C group (P < 0.001 and P < 0.01, respectively). No differences were determined between groups in liver or plasma triglyceride and cholesterol levels, SMA blood flow, intestinal villus height, crypt depth, or overall intestinal morphology. Hepatic and intestinal protein synthesis rates and in vivo bile acid clearance were also not significantly different between groups. Co-supplementation of PN with vitamins E and C was associated with lower hepatic oxidative stress and steatosis in neonatal piglets. Although no improvements were measured in intestinal structure or perfusion, these findings support the potential of antioxidant-enriched PN formulations to mitigate PN-associated liver complications.

title: The Dietary Polyphenol Epigallocatechin Gallate Delays Biological Aging by Activating Peroxisome Biogenesis and Peroxisomal Fatty Acid β-Oxidation.
label: approved
note: Tea polyphenol EGCG and biological ageing.
abstract: Epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG), a major tea polyphenol, has been proposed to promote healthy aging, but population-level evidence and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We analyzed 10,977 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) and conducted mechanistic studies in Caenorhabditis elegans and AML12 hepatocytes. Compared with non-consumers, both lower and higher EGCG intake categories were associated with lower PhenoAge acceleration, lower all-cause mortality, and higher estimated residual life expectancy. In C. elegans, EGCG supplementation extended lifespan and health span. Transcriptomics revealed upregulation of peroxisome-related genes. EGCG enhanced peroxisome biogenesis, as shown by increased peroxisome abundance, elevated prx-5 and prx-19 mRNA levels, and increases in PRX-5 and PRX-19 proteins. This increase in peroxisome capacity was accompanied by enhanced peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidation, with increased mRNA levels of acox-1.2, acox-3, and dhs-28, increased ACOX-3 protein, and reduced very long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs). Lipidomics showed enhanced processing of VLCFAs and accumulation of shorter-chain intermediates. Knockdown of prx-5, acox-1.2, or dhs-28 abolished EGCG-induced lifespan and health span benefits. In doxorubicin-induced senescent AML12 hepatocytes, EGCG reduced the proportion of SA-β-gal-positive cells and decreased p21 and p16 protein levels, while increasing peroxisome abundance and peroxisome-related proteins, including the biogenesis factors PEX5 and PEX19, the membrane transporters ABCD1 and PMP70, and the β-oxidation enzymes ACOX1, HSD17B4, EHHADH, and ACAA1. Conversely, the anti-senescent effects of EGCG were attenuated by Pex5 or Acox1 knockdown. Collectively, dietary EGCG intake is associated with slower biological aging, while experimental findings support peroxisome biogenesis and peroxisomal fatty acid β-oxidation in EGCG-mediated anti-aging effects.
